official_measurement_examples.fact: The Environment Agency published a replacement odour-management guidance set on 3 December 2025 for regulated activities and environmental permits.
An environmental permit can require an odour risk assessment and an approved odour management plan where necessary.
Permit odour conditions focus on preventing or minimising odour pollution outside the site using appropriate measures.
Odour assessment is receptor- and site-specific and can use monitoring, reports, source character and operational evidence; a generic buffer is not a measured impact.
An odour management plan is a management and compliance document, not proof that no odour impact will occur.
Environmental permitting and planning are separate regimes; permit approval does not itself grant planning permission and planning permission does not replace permit conditions.
Predicted or modelled odour evidence must not be silently treated as post-operation measured receptor impact.
Odour-permit status does not establish ownership, planning acceptability, nuisance immunity, infrastructure capacity or development yield.

core_rules: permit odour condition is not planning permission
planning permission is not permit compliance
generic buffer is not measured impact
predicted odour is not measured receptor impact
permit compliance must retain time period
odour permit does not establish ownership
odour control does not prove nuisance immunity
permit does not establish infrastructure capacity
permit does not calculate development yield
current 2025 guidance supersedes retired H4 assumptions for EA England context
no parcel odour clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
